verdict_reasoning: No level fails. The only surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is a fixable design point: v3 documents product(real) as returning double precision, while sum(real) returns real, and the thread says the two match. Demand is supported by the report in message #10 that the next SQL standard requires PRODUCT. A committer is already listed on the CommitFest entry.

brief.title: Add a built-in product() aggregate
brief.problem: Postgres has sum() but no aggregate that multiplies values, for example to compound growth factors or combine probabilities. Users today write a custom aggregate or use exp(sum(ln(x))), which fails for zero or negative inputs and loses precision.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds product() for int2, int4, int8, float4, float8 and numeric, and it ignores nulls like sum(). Integer and numeric inputs accumulate in numeric and return numeric. Since v3, float4 and float8 inputs accumulate in float8 and return double precision; the aggregate supports parallel combine but has no inverse transition function for moving windows.
user_visible_surface: New aggregate product(smallint | integer | bigint | numeric) returning numeric.
New aggregate product(real | double precision) returning double precision (v3; v1 returned numeric).
New support functions in pg_proc: int2/int4/int8/float4_product_accum.
product() returns null for an empty input or an all-null group.
A finite float product that overflows double precision raises an error; Infinity appears only if it is in the input.
author_claims: Common request; exp(sum(ln())) breaks on zero and negative inputs and is imprecise.
Per-type variants give exact integer results, where implicit casts would pick float8 and lose precision.
A native int64/int128 fast path helps little, because products overflow bigint within a few rows.
Float return type now matches sum(float4)/sum(float8).
Proposed by Peter Eisentraut; regression tests cover NULLs, DISTINCT, FILTER, NaN/Infinity, overflow, parallel and window use.
brief.thread_state: Vaibhav Dalvi said v3 looks good with no more comments, and Peter Eisentraut is listed as committer. Vik Fearing says the next SQL standard requires PRODUCT(col, 1 ON EMPTY), and Tom Lane asked to treat that as a separate feature in Jeevan's other ON EMPTY thread.
unclear: Nobody has said whether product() should ship before the standard's ON EMPTY syntax, or wait for it.
Dean Rasheed has not said whether he accepts the per-type variants after Jeevan's reply.
The thread gives no performance numbers for product() compared with sum() or exp(sum(ln())).
The commit message does not say whether product(float4) returning float8 differs from sum(float4), which returns real.
Nobody has said whether the name product could conflict with user-defined functions in existing databases.

objections.title: product(real) returns double precision while sum(real) returns real
objections.failure_scenario: A user writes a query or view with sum(r) and product(r) over a real column, expecting both results to be real like the input. The product column comes back as double precision. This changes the result type of views, the types that drivers bind, and the output of CREATE TABLE AS. The user finds out only when inspecting column types or when client code checks them.
objections.argument: Message #26 asked for the float variants to match sum(float4)/sum(float8), and messages #27 and #28 state that v3 matches them. But sum(float4) returns real, and v3 documents product(real) as returning double precision. A float8 transition state may be justified because products overflow real quickly. Even so, the commit message and docs do not say that the result type departs from sum(), and the claim of consistency in the thread is not accurate for real.
objections.author_must_show: Should product(real) return real like sum(real), and if not, can the docs and commit message state the difference and the reason for it?

critic.reasoning: sum(real) returns real, and v3 documents product(real) as returning double precision, so the statement in messages #27 and #28 that v3 matches sum() is inaccurate for real. The signature table shows the type, but no text gives the reason for the difference.

refuted.title: New built-in name can take over existing user product() aggregates
refuted.failure_scenario: A site has its own public.product(float8) or product(numeric) aggregate, perhaps one that returns 1 on empty input. After upgrade, pg_catalog comes first in the search path, so unqualified product(x) in ad hoc queries and new views resolves to the built-in. These calls now return null for empty groups or a different type. Existing views keep the old OID, so the database ends up mixing both behaviours.
refuted.argument: product is the obvious name for a user-written multiplying aggregate, and message #1 says users write custom aggregates today. Adding built-in names is normal practice in Postgres, so this does not block the feature. It does call for a release-note compatibility item, and the proposal does not mention one. The brief lists this as unaddressed in the thread.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the patch add a release-note compatibility item for databases that already define a product aggregate with matching argument types?

critic.reasoning: Every new built-in function can shadow a user function of the same name, and Postgres accepts this routinely, as the objection itself concedes. Release notes are written at release time from commit messages, so a patch is not expected to carry a compatibility item.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds pg_proc and pg_aggregate rows and needs a CATALOG_VERSION_NO bump.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: Message #10 says the next SQL standard defines PRODUCT with an ON EMPTY clause, which this patch leaves to another thread.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: An existing user aggregate named product with the same argument types is shadowed by the pg_catalog one after upgrade.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Six aggregate variants and four new accumulator functions in numeric.c stay in core for good.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: A user can already create the same aggregate with numeric_mul as transition and combine function.

questions: Should product(real) return real like sum(real), and if not, can the docs and commit message state the difference and the reason?
Should product() be committed before the standard's ON EMPTY syntax, or wait for the other thread?
Does Dean Rasheed accept the per-type integer variants after the reply about exact integer results?
How does product() compare in speed with sum() and with exp(sum(ln(x))) on the same data?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut proposed the idea and is listed as committer on the CommitFest entry; the work needs someone who knows the numeric and float aggregate code.
committability.liability: The name product, its result types and its null result on empty input become permanent SQL surface. They must stay compatible with the standard's PRODUCT once ON EMPTY is added.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted three versions and answered each review, per messages #5, #9 and #28.

priority.reason: The patch adds catalog rows and small accumulator functions that reuse numeric_mul and float8mul, and costs nothing for users who do not call product(). A committer is listed and a reviewer has no more comments on v3; the open point is the result type for real.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the accumulator functions' null handling, float overflow checks and parallel combine behaviour are unverified. Only 3 of 29 messages were visible, so later agreement or disagreement in the thread may be missing.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: onlyvalue aggregate
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a core aggregate function (initially named "onlyvalue", later discussed as "single_value" or "unique_value") that returns the single value present in its input group and raises an error if the group contains more than one distinct value. It is meant as a self-checking, self-documenting replacement for using min() or max() on columns expected to be constant within a group.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed's review of v2 found bugs (a server crash in null handling, a cache lookup failure with complex types) and asked for more comments, a change to the finalfn call order and collation handling. The author did not post a new version for more than a month, so the commitfest manager marked the patch returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There is a review, but no input from the author for more than 1 month,
hence patch has been marked as "returned with feedback".

precedents_retrieved.title: Partial aggregates push down
precedents_retrieved.summary: postgres_fdw pushes partial aggregation to the remote server for aggregates marked safe by a new pg_aggregate flag (set for min/max/sum/count). For aggregates with internal state, a new converter function runs locally and turns the remote aggregate result into the local partial-aggregate state.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra was still not convinced of the approach in the last review. He saw no clear path to aggregates with complex states such as avg(), and he doubted that the aggpartialpushdownsafe flag without version checks ensures the remote node represents the state the same way. The author agreed he did not know how to handle complex states, and postgres_fdw has no way to learn the remote server version at planning time. The visible messages do not show further discussion before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
1) It's not clear to me how could this get extended to aggregates with
more complex aggregate states, to support e.g. avg() and similar fairly
common aggregates.

precedents_retrieved.title: Partial aggregates push down
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let postgres_fdw push partial aggregation down to remote servers, so each shard computes a partial aggregate state and the local server finalizes it. Early versions handled simple aggregates such as count, min, max and sum, and later versions extended this to aggregates with internal states, using added partial aggregate functions and a remote version check.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas said two major areas of work remained before the feature could be committed. Approach #2, which does the pushdown with an SQL keyword instead of separate partial aggregate functions for each aggregate, still needed investigation. Sending serialized bytea states between servers that cannot fully trust each other also needed design work and consensus. The entry closed as returned with feedback because, as vignesh C wrote, there was "still some work" left.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In addition, the problems around transmitting serialized bytea blobs between machines that can't be assumed to fully trust each other will need to be addressed in some way, which seems like it will require a good deal of design work, forming some kind of consensus, and then implementation work to follow.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize numeric comparison and aggregation via packed-datum extraction
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch speeds up numeric min, max, sum, avg and variance by reading numeric fields directly from packed (1-byte header) datums, so that each row no longer needs a detoast with palloc and memcpy. min and max return the original input Datum, and the accumulation functions use a new init_var_from_packed().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the author posted: a v2 patch fixed a CFBot alignment failure on strict architectures, and no reviewer reply appears in the thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Partial aggregates push down
precedents_retrieved.summary: Push partial aggregation down to remote servers through postgres_fdw, so each shard computes a partial aggregate state and the local server combines and finalizes the states. The first version allowed only simple aggregates such as count, max, min and sum, chosen by name, and later work tried to extend it to aggregates with an internal state type, such as avg.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages show no agreed method for sending partial states of aggregates with an internal state type, such as avg(bigint), avg(numeric) or avg(interval). The thread compared new export functions, new data types such as int128, and a record built from a list of type OIDs. Tomas Vondra said serial/deserial functions are not stable across releases. He also said that limiting pushdown to the same minor version would block it during node-by-node upgrades. The visible messages contain no closing message, and Bruce Momjian wrote that the docs were on hold until a transfer method was chosen.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For serial/deserial we make no guarantees, it can change even in a minor release. But here we need something stable even for major releases, to allow pushdown when querying older server.

precedents_retrieved.title: Push down aggregates below joins.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves aggregate planning from grouping_planner() into scan/join planning, so the planner can build a grouped RelOptInfo for each scan or join rel and place the Agg node below a join. Antonin Houska's related patch, merged into the same discussion, also supports splitting into a partial aggregate below the join and a final aggregate above it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was returned because it waited for a new version from its author for about two months. The last posted version was incomplete: it did not yet check whether a join duplicates grouping keys, it failed on cases such as grouping by a column derived through an equivalence class, and it did not handle binary equality of grouping keys. Earlier, Peter Eisentraut reported merge conflicts, partition_aggregate test failures and a missing expected output file.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting for input from its author for a couple of
months now, so I am switching it to "Returned with Feedback".

precedents_retrieved.title: Add numeric_trim(numeric)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Dean Rasheed, Alvaro Herrera, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a function numeric_trim(numeric) that removes trailing zeros after the decimal point by lowering the value's display scale. Reviewers also discussed a minscale() function that returns the smallest scale needed, to be used with round().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed found a bug: numeric_trim(1e100) fails with "value overflows numeric format" because the computed dscale goes negative. He also asked for a simpler implementation based on strip_var(), and the thread moved toward a minscale() design. The author did not post a new version, so Alvaro Herrera and later Robert Haas closed the entry as returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this patch got useful feedback but we never saw a followup
version posted.  I closed it as returned-with-feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Precision loss casting float to numeric
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Robert Haas, Bear Giles
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make the float4 and float8 to numeric casts keep full binary precision, so that the cast and the round trip back to float no longer lose bits. The proof-of-concept patch printed values with FLT_DECIMAL_DIG and DBL_DECIMAL_DIG digits in place of FLT_DIG and DBL_DIG, and the author planned a frexp-based conversion.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Robert Haas expected more complaints about results such as 1.1::float8 casting to an odd-looking numeric than benefit from exact values, and Bear Giles asked that existing results not change. Making the cast follow extra_float_digits would make it stable instead of immutable. Per-schema casts cannot work because casts have no names, which left a separate named function as the remaining option. The author marked the entry Returned with feedback, citing the backward-compatibility issues and lack of time in this CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think there's probably a bigger chance of complaints that "casting 1.1::float8 to numeric now produces some weird, incorrectly-rounded result" than that we make anyone happier.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The only listed precedent [P1] is a different aggregate, onlyvalue, returned for lack of author follow-up on review bugs. That reason does not apply here: the author answered each review in message #5, #9 and #28. The thread points to the author's separate ON EMPTY patch (message #11, #17), not to an earlier product() attempt.

The standard's PRODUCT(x, 1 ON EMPTY) is defined as COALESCE(PRODUCT(x), 1), per message #22. Plain product() returning null on empty input fits that definition, so shipping it before ON EMPTY creates no conflict.

The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL record or protocol message, and adds no ABI-visible struct; its persistent state is new pg_proc and pg_aggregate rows plus a catversion bump. A user aggregate named product with the same signature would be shadowed after pg_upgrade by the pg_catalog version, as with any new built-in, and the proposal does not say whether this was checked.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. product() is a plain built-in aggregate over numeric and float types, executable by anyone like sum(), and it reads only rows the caller can already see. Its cost is bounded by the numeric size limit, and an existing custom aggregate built on numeric_mul gives the same cost to any user today.

From the maintenance angle the proposal adds catalog rows that reuse numeric_mul and float8mul, with no hot-path cost for non-users and no new API or dependency; Peter Eisentraut is the listed committer. Shadowing of existing user-defined product() aggregates is a risk shared by every new built-in function, and the ON EMPTY syntax was split off by message #12.

A user can already write `create aggregate product(numeric) (sfunc = numeric_mul, stype = numeric, combinefunc = numeric_mul)`, so core adds convenience only. Message #10 says the next SQL standard requires PRODUCT, and a committer proposed the feature, so this objection would likely not be sent. Not checked: how upgraded databases with their own public.product() behave once pg_catalog.product() is found first.

The thread shows enough demand: message #10 reports that the next SQL standard edition requires PRODUCT, and a committer proposed the idea. The cost is a few pg_proc and pg_aggregate rows that only callers of product() use, and the exp(sum(ln())) workaround fails on zero and negative inputs.
